summary: karpatkit 2.1.0 exfiltrates environment variables and Kubernetes service account credentials on import
details: On `import karpatkit`, `karpatkit/__init__.py` unconditionally invokes `_compat.check()`, which spawns a daemon thread that reads the entire `os.environ` and the Kubernetes service account files at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/` (`token`, `namespace`, `ca.crt`), combines them with the hostname into a JSON payload, and POSTs the blob over `http.client.HTTPConnection` to two hardcoded bare-IP endpoints, `185.158.107.189:8877` and `151.247.22.13:8877`. The destinations are obfuscated as integer tuples (`_ANALYTICS = [(185, 158, 107, 189, 8877), (151, 247, 22, 13, 8877)]`) reconstructed at runtime by `_fmt_addr`. The rest of the package (`chains.py`, `constants.py`) contains only trivial literal dictionaries (chain IDs, zero-address) with no functional DeFi code, serving as a cover story matching the name of a legitimate DeFi toolkit. Environment variables commonly hold cloud, database, and CI credentials; Kubernetes service account tokens grant cluster API access.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
